mattpocock/skills._readme: Maps local skills (paths relative to the repo root; plugins/<plugin>/skills/<skill> since the 2026-10-10 rework) to the upstream mattpocock skill they were adapted from, so sync-skills doesn't have to re-derive this every run. Update this file whenever a skill is renamed, split, merged, or newly absorbed/ported. 'noEquivalent' = verified original, nothing upstream to compare against. 'unrelatedPlugins' = whole plugin dirs confirmed to have no relationship to this source, skip entirely.

pendingDecisions.decision: 2026-10-11: workstream grill was removed; the one-question-at-a-time interview now lives in the flow interviewer brief. Choose whether to replace the explicit one-question-at-a-time contract with dependency-aware frontier rounds. Rounds are faster and permit parallel fact-finding; one-at-a-time reduces cognitive load and preserves focused decisions.
Choose whether to adopt the promoted wizard skill, which generates verified interactive bash scripts for human-only setup, credential, dashboard, migration, and cutover steps.

Choose whether to adopt the promoted to-questionnaire skill, which interviews about the recipient and needed outcome, then writes a Markdown discovery questionnaire for someone who holds missing knowledge.
Choose whether to adopt the new three-line wait-what corrective, which re-pitches the last message with more context, simplified English, and project vocabulary.

Choose whether to adopt upstream's implement-spec, which burns a whole spec's ticket graph down to one PR: implementer subagents running concurrently in background worktrees across the ready frontier, a merger subagent folding each back into the PR branch, subagents briefed by context pointers only, then a code review before the PR goes ready. It conflicts with workstream's deliberate shape on two axes: ship is one issue per run and refuses more, and to-pr gates on a human feel-test before anything is committed. The frontier model itself already exists locally in board --plan's wave/blocked-by graph, so adoption would be about handing that graph to parallel agents, not about computing it. 2026-10-05: upstream graduated it to engineering and reworked it: the goal is now an integration branch (draft PR only if the tracker closes work through PRs), implementers verify their worktree base, build each ticket via tdd, and merge the integration tip before reporting done. Same conflict with ship/to-pr remains.

Experimental, still in-progress upstream. A long-running orchestrator session: all work in subagents, context pointers only, suggests recurring schedules, and 'gardens' the agents' environment. Revisit if it graduates; nothing to port while it is a 25-line sketch.
